stays.name: Riad Yasmina: Courtyard Pool in the Mouassine Medina

host.name: Youssef
host.presence: A housekeeper and cook are on site daily; Youssef greets every guest at check-in with mint tea on the roof terrace.

highlights.title: Top 5% of homes
highlights.detail: This home is highly ranked based on ratings, reviews, and reliability.

highlights.title: Dive right in
highlights.detail: This is one of the few places in the medina with a private courtyard plunge pool.

highlights.title: Greeted at the door
highlights.detail: A member of the riad team walks you in from the nearest taxi drop-off — no getting lost in the derbs.

stays.description: A classic 18th-century riad in the Mouassine quarter, restored over three years by local maalems. The central courtyard holds a small turquoise-tiled plunge pool shaded by orange trees, and every salon opens onto it through carved cedar doors. Breakfast of msemen, amlou, and fresh orange juice is served on the roof terrace with Koutoubia views. The Secret Garden and the souks are three minutes on foot.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation before August 1. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Sophie
reviews.text: The riad is even more beautiful than the photos. We spent every afternoon by the courtyard pool after mornings in the souks, and the team's breakfast on the roof was the best meal we had in Marrakech. Youssef arranged everything from airport transfer to a cooking class.

reviews.author: Daniel
reviews.text: Six of us had the whole riad and it felt like a private hotel. The rooms are gorgeous — carved cedar, zellige everywhere — and it stays remarkably cool and quiet despite being three minutes from the souks.

reviews.author: Amira
reviews.text: Being met at the taxi and walked through the derbs was such a relief on arrival. The plunge pool is small but genuinely swimmable and the orange trees smell incredible in spring.

reviews.author: Tom
reviews.text: One of the best places I have stayed anywhere. The courtyard at night with the lanterns lit is unforgettable. Book the in-riad dinner at least once — the tagine was superb.

Decorative fountain in the middle of a riad courtyard
Ornate wooden door opening to a tiled hallway
Moroccan sitting room with planters and a patterned rug
Intricate geometric zellige mosaic tile pattern

stays.name: Dar El Fna: Historic House Steps from Jemaa el-Fnaa

host.name: Fatima-Zahra
host.work: Family-run guesthouses in the old medina
host.presence: My brother Mehdi manages check-in and can arrange guides, drivers, and restaurant bookings.

highlights.title: The square on your doorstep
highlights.detail: Two minutes on foot from Jemaa el-Fnaa, yet tucked down a quiet dead-end derb.

highlights.title: Cool marble salon
highlights.detail: Columned ground-floor salon with a checkerboard marble floor stays cool through the summer.

highlights.title: Self check-in
highlights.detail: Check yourself in with the lockbox after Mehdi's welcome call.

stays.description: A traditional family dar a short walk from Jemaa el-Fnaa, on a quiet cul-de-sac derb that shuts out the noise of the square. The ground floor keeps its original columned salon with checkerboard marble, and the small dipping pool in the light well is a lifesaver in August. At night, climb to the terrace to hear the drummers on the square and watch the smoke rise from the food stalls.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation for 48 hours. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Lucas
reviews.text: You cannot beat this location. We watched the square come alive every evening from the terrace and were asleep in silence ten minutes later. Mehdi's restaurant tips were all winners.

reviews.author: Ingrid
reviews.text: The marble salon downstairs is stunning and genuinely cool even at midday. The house is old and full of character — expect steep riad stairs — and we loved it.

reviews.author: Karim
reviews.text: Perfect base with children: close to everything, the little pool was a hit, and the dead-end alley meant no scooters. Fatima-Zahra checked in on us throughout.

reviews.author: Hannah
reviews.text: Beautiful, atmospheric house in an unbeatable spot. Wifi dropped a couple of times on the terrace but was fine indoors. Would happily return.

stays.name: Villa des Oliviers: Palmeraie Estate with Heated Pool

host.name: Leïla
host.presence: A full staff — cook, gardener, and house manager — is included; Leïla plans menus with guests before arrival.

highlights.title: Staffed villa
highlights.detail: Cook, gardener, and house manager included in the rate; in-villa dinners on request.

highlights.title: Heated pool in an olive garden
highlights.detail: Seventeen-meter pool surrounded by centenary olive trees and palms.

highlights.title: Free parking on premises
highlights.detail: Gated estate with room for three cars; 20 minutes to the medina.

stays.description: A pisé-walled estate deep in the Palmeraie, set in two hectares of olive trees, palms, and bougainvillea. Five en-suite bedrooms open onto shaded loggias, and the 17-meter heated pool looks toward the Atlas on clear mornings. Rachida's kitchen — from Friday couscous to poolside kefta — is reason enough to stay in for dinner. Quiet, green, and a world away from the medina, which is a 20-minute drive.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation before August 15. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Charlotte
reviews.text: Three generations of our family stayed a week and nobody wanted to leave. Rachida's cooking was extraordinary, the pool was warm even in the evenings, and the garden is full of birdsong.

reviews.author: James
reviews.text: Flawless. The house manager arranged drivers into the medina whenever we wanted, and coming back to a quiet olive grove after the souks was the perfect rhythm.

reviews.author: Nour
reviews.text: Leïla's design taste is impeccable — every room is calm and beautiful. Sunset by the pool with the Atlas in the distance is something I will not forget.

reviews.author: Oliver
reviews.text: Wonderful villa and staff. You do need a car or drivers for everything, which we knew going in. Dinners at the villa beat most restaurants we tried in town.

images.alt: Large swimming pool with lounge chairs around it
Villa swimming pool in bright sunlight
White villa facade behind green palm trees
Light-filled living room with layered textiles
Earthen kasbah walls rising behind palm trees

stays.name: Sunny Art-Deco Apartment with Balcony in Gueliz
stays.typeLabel: Entire rental unit in Marrakech, Morocco

host.name: Amine
host.presence: Self check-in with a smart lock; I live two streets away and can drop by if anything is needed.

highlights.title: New-town convenience
highlights.detail: Cafés, galleries, and the Carré Eden supermarket are all under five minutes on foot.

highlights.title: Art-deco bones
highlights.detail: 1930s building with original terrazzo floors and a wraparound balcony over Rue de la Liberté.

highlights.title: Self check-in
highlights.detail: Check yourself in with the smart lock.

stays.description: A bright one-bedroom in a 1930s art-deco block in the heart of Gueliz, Marrakech's new town. Original terrazzo floors, rattan furniture, and a balcony made for morning coffee above the jacaranda trees. Majorelle Garden is a 15-minute walk, the medina a 10-minute taxi. Ideal for travelers who want café life and gallery-hopping alongside the souks.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation for 48 hours. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Elena
reviews.text: Exactly what we wanted — a calm, stylish base in the new town. Walking to Majorelle before the crowds was easy, and the balcony breakfast spot is lovely.

reviews.author: Mark
reviews.text: Great value and a genuinely charming building. Amine's café list for Gueliz was excellent. Taxis to the medina were cheap and quick.

reviews.author: Salma
reviews.text: Comfortable and spotless. Some street noise in the early evening, as you would expect in Gueliz, but quiet by night. Would stay again.

images.alt: Bright white apartment interior with wooden accents
Leather sofa with a wooden frame in a sunlit room
Wooden dining set on a sunny terrace
Green palm tree beside a white and blue building
People sitting on wooden café chairs in the sun

stays.name: Dar Zitoun: Restored Dar by the Bahia Palace
stays.location: Riad Zitoun Jdid, Marrakech Medina, Morocco

host.name: Rachid
host.presence: I restored the cedar ceilings and doors myself; I am usually nearby and happy to share the house's story.

highlights.title: Palace quarter
highlights.detail: Bahia Palace, Dar Si Said, and the Mellah spice market are all within a five-minute walk.

highlights.title: Craftsman's restoration
highlights.detail: Hand-painted cedar ceilings and zellige restored by the host, a working maalem.

highlights.title: Quiet double-patio layout
highlights.detail: Two internal patios keep the bedrooms silent and full of light.

stays.description: A patient, craftsman-led restoration of a family dar in the palace quarter, between the Bahia Palace and the Mellah. Rachid rebuilt the painted cedar ceilings and cut the zellige panels in his own workshop. Two small patios — one with a fig tree, one with a fountain — bring light into every room. The Saadian Tombs and the spice souk of the Mellah are minutes away on foot.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation before August 1. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Isabelle
reviews.text: Staying in a house restored by the craftsman himself is something special. Rachid walked us through every ceiling and door — the detail is museum-quality. Perfect location for the palaces.

reviews.author: Ben
reviews.text: Our kids loved the fig-tree patio and we loved how quiet the bedrooms were. Bahia Palace before opening crowds was a two-minute stroll.

reviews.author: Chiara
reviews.text: Extraordinary value for this level of beauty. The fountain patio at breakfast, the painted ceilings at night — it is a privilege to stay here.

images.alt: Person standing at the opened carved door of a Moroccan house
Brown and white horseshoe arches in a courtyard

Colorful geometric mosaic tile pattern

stays.name: Agafay Desert Lodge Tent with Atlas Views

host.name: Hassan
host.work: Founder of a small eco-camp in the Agafay
host.presence: Our Berber team lives at the camp; dinners are cooked over fire and every stay includes a sunset camel walk.

highlights.title: Desert one hour from town
highlights.detail: The stone desert of Agafay is a 60-minute drive from the medina — no long Sahara transfer needed.

highlights.title: Dinner under the stars
highlights.detail: Three-course Berber dinner by the fire pit and breakfast at sunrise are included.

highlights.title: Off-grid, thoughtfully
highlights.detail: Solar power, private bathroom with hot water, and zero light pollution for stargazing.

stays.description: A private lodge tent in a small eco-camp on a ridge of the Agafay, Marrakech's moonscape stone desert. Inside: a proper king bed, Berber rugs, and an en-suite bathroom with hot water; outside, a private terrace facing the snow lines of the Atlas. Days end with a camel walk to the sunset dune, dinner by the fire, and a sky thick with stars. The medina is an hour away, but it will feel like another planet.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation before August 10. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Priya
reviews.text: The single best night of our Morocco trip. Dinner by the fire, drumming, then total silence and the Milky Way. The tent is genuinely luxurious — hot shower and the most comfortable bed.

reviews.author: Stefan
reviews.text: We almost skipped the desert because we didn't have time for the Sahara. So glad we found this — one hour from Marrakech and completely otherworldly. The sunset camel walk was beautiful, not touristy.

reviews.author: Aya
reviews.text: Cold January night, warm blankets, hot tagine, endless stars. Hassan's team could not have been kinder.

reviews.author: George
reviews.text: Magical experience. The track in is rough for the last twenty minutes — take their driver rather than a rental car. Otherwise perfect.

stays.name: Ourika Valley Riverside Lodge with Mountain Terrace

host.name: Khadija
host.work: Runs a women's argan cooperative in the valley
host.presence: My family lives next door; we bring fresh bread and can cook dinner on request.

highlights.title: River at the garden gate
highlights.detail: The Ourika river runs directly below the terrace — fall asleep to the water.

highlights.title: Cool mountain air
highlights.detail: Ten degrees cooler than Marrakech in summer, 45 minutes from the city.

highlights.title: Home cooking
highlights.detail: Khadija's family cooks valley tagines and fresh bread on request.

stays.description: A stone-and-pisé lodge on the banks of the Ourika river, 45 minutes from Marrakech and ten degrees cooler in summer. The terrace hangs over the water with the High Atlas rising behind walnut and cherry orchards. Hike to the Setti Fatma waterfalls, visit Khadija's argan cooperative, or do nothing at all with a pot of mint tea and the sound of the river.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation for 48 hours. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Mathilde
reviews.text: Escaping the June heat of Marrakech to this terrace above the river was heaven. Khadija's mother's couscous is the best meal we ate in Morocco, no contest.

reviews.author: David
reviews.text: Kids paddled in the river, we drank tea in the hammocks, and the waterfall hike from Setti Fatma was a highlight. Very easy 45-minute drive from the city.

reviews.author: Rania
reviews.text: The sound of the river all night is the best sleep aid there is. Visiting the argan cooperative was fascinating — go with Khadija if she offers.

reviews.author: Peter
reviews.text: Rustic in the best way — thick blankets, fireplace lit for us each evening. Wifi is valley wifi; plan accordingly and enjoy the disconnection.

stays.name: Imlil Eco-Lodge: Toubkal Views and Walnut Groves

host.name: Brahim
host.work: Certified mountain guide, born in Imlil
host.presence: I grew up in this valley and guide Toubkal treks; my family runs the lodge while I am on the mountain.

highlights.title: Trailhead location
highlights.detail: The classic Toubkal route and the Tizi n'Tamatert day hike both start at the door.

highlights.title: Hosted by a mountain guide
highlights.detail: Brahim arranges mules, permits, and guided summits at honest local rates.

highlights.title: Terrace above the walnut groves
highlights.detail: Sunset light on Jbel Toubkal from the rooftop, tea in hand.

stays.description: A simple, warm stone lodge at 1,740 meters in Imlil, the trekking village at the foot of Jbel Toubkal, North Africa's highest peak. Wood stoves, thick Berber blankets, and a rooftop terrace looking straight up the valley to the summit snows. Brahim — a certified guide born here — arranges everything from gentle village walks among the walnut groves to two-day Toubkal ascents.
amenities: Free parking in the village lot

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation for 48 hours. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Jonas
reviews.text: Brahim organized our Toubkal summit flawlessly — mules, refuge booking, everything. Coming back to the wood stove and his mother's harira was the perfect end to the climb.

reviews.author: Alice
reviews.text: You don't need to be a climber to love this place. We did easy walks through the walnut groves and villages, and the terrace view of the snowy summit is constant magic.

reviews.author: Miguel
reviews.text: Honest, warm, and spectacularly located. Cold nights but the blankets and stove more than cope. Best 86 dollars a night in Morocco.

images.alt: Berber village houses stacked on a brown hillside
Villages perched on the edge of an Atlas mountainside
Bird's eye view of a High Atlas mountain peak
Traditional earthen-brick village in the mountains
Aerial view of folded brown Atlas mountains

stays.name: Riad Atlas Rooftop: Plunge Pool and Koutoubia Views

host.name: Samira
host.work: Runs three riads with her sisters
host.presence: Our house team is in the riad from 8am to 8pm; rooftop dinners can be booked a day ahead.

highlights.title: A rooftop made for evenings
highlights.detail: Lantern-lit terrace with a tiled plunge pool and a clear line to the Koutoubia minaret.

highlights.title: Room for the whole group
highlights.detail: Four en-suite bedrooms around the patio — rent it and the house is entirely yours.

highlights.title: Self check-in
highlights.detail: Check yourself in with the lockbox; the team greets you next morning with breakfast.

stays.description: A generous four-bedroom riad near Bab Doukkala with the best rooftop in its price range: rugs, lanterns, a tiled plunge pool, and the Koutoubia minaret on the skyline. Bedrooms are set around a banana-palm patio, each with its own tadelakt bathroom. The food souk of Bab Doukkala — where locals actually shop — is around the corner, and taxis can reach the door, a rarity in the medina.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation before August 5. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Nadia
reviews.text: Eight of us for a birthday weekend and it was perfect. Sunset on that rooftop with the call to prayer echoing across the medina — chills. The team's rooftop dinner was better than any restaurant we booked.

reviews.author: Will
reviews.text: Taxi access to the door sounds like a small thing until you've dragged luggage through the souks. Brilliantly run riad, spotless rooms, and the plunge pool got daily use.

reviews.author: Francesca
reviews.text: Samira and her sisters run a tight ship. Breakfast on the roof — msemen, eggs, fruit, endless coffee — set up every day of our stay.

reviews.author: Adam
reviews.text: Lovely riad, great value for four couples. Bab Doukkala is more local and less polished than the central medina, which we ended up preferring.

images.alt: Colorful textiles hanging on a Marrakech rooftop
Wooden table and chairs on a rooftop terrace
Koutoubia minaret rising above Marrakech

stays.name: Kasbah-Style Country House above Lake Takerkoust
stays.typeLabel: Entire home in Lalla Takerkoust, Morocco

host.name: Omar
host.work: Built the house with local pisé masons over four years
host.presence: A caretaker couple lives on the property; I visit most weekends and love showing guests the lake.

highlights.title: Newly opened
highlights.detail: Hand-built pisé kasbah finished in 2025, hosting guests since early 2026.

highlights.title: Lake and Atlas panorama
highlights.detail: Rooftop crenellations look over Lake Takerkoust to the High Atlas wall.

highlights.title: Between desert and mountains
highlights.detail: Agafay desert 20 minutes one way, Atlas foothill trails 20 minutes the other.

stays.description: A new country house built the old way — rammed pisé earth, palm-beam ceilings, and a crenellated roof terrace in the style of the southern kasbahs. It stands on a low hill above Lake Takerkoust, 45 minutes from Marrakech, between the Agafay desert and the first ridges of the Atlas. Swim in the small courtyard pool, ride horses along the lakeshore, and grill dinner under a sky with no city glow.

houseRules.cancellation: Free cancellation for 48 hours. Cancel before check-in for a partial refund.

reviews.author: Camille
reviews.text: The house itself is the experience — cool earthen walls, that castle rooftop, sunset over the lake. We did Agafay quads one day and an Atlas hike the next, both twenty minutes away.

reviews.author: Reda
reviews.text: Omar's caretakers were wonderful with our kids and lit the outdoor oven for a bread-baking morning. Feels remote but Marrakech is an easy 45-minute drive.

reviews.author: Laura
reviews.text: Beautiful, atmospheric new build with a few new-house quirks — hot water took a while one morning. The views and silence more than make up for it.

images.alt: Kasbah walls and towers behind palm trees
Rocky Atlas mountain under a clear blue sky
Wooden table and chairs on a sunny terrace
Building interior with rows of Moorish arches
Potted green plant in front of a traditional doorway

experiences.name: Souk food tour with a medina-born guide

host.name: Abdellah
host.bio: Born two alleys from the spice souk, Abdellah has eaten at the same msemen stall for thirty years. Former cook, full-time storyteller, and on first-name terms with every vendor on the route.

experiences.description: Eat your way through the real medina: msemen off the griddle, olives and preserved lemons in the Mellah market, sheep's-milk jben, snail broth if you dare, and a rooftop mint tea to finish. Ten-plus tastings at stalls locals actually queue for, with the history of each quarter told between bites.

images.alt: People walking through a busy medina street
Woven baskets stacked on display in the souk
Man holding a bowl of freshly prepared Moroccan food

experiences.name: Tagine cooking class in a riad kitchen

host.name: Latifa
host.bio: Dada-trained home cook who ran the kitchen of a Mouassine guesthouse for fifteen years. Teaches the dishes of her grandmother's Friday table from her own riad kitchen.

experiences.description: Shop the market for saffron, preserved lemon, and the day's vegetables, then build a proper tagine from the base up — plus taktouka salad and fresh khobz baked in the neighborhood ferran, the communal wood oven. Lunch is eaten together on the patio, recipes sent home with you.

images.alt: Steaming tagine dish served at the table
Rows of clay tagine pots on display
Spread of Moroccan dishes served on a table

experiences.name: Traditional hammam and black-soap ritual

host.name: Najat
host.bio: Third-generation hammam attendant whose grandmother worked the same neighborhood bathhouse. Now leads private rituals in a restored 17th-century hammam near the Mouassine fountain.

experiences.description: The full ritual, done properly and privately: steam under a star-pierced dome, beldi black soap, a serious kessa-glove scrub, rhassoul clay from the Atlas, and orange-blossom tea in the cool room after. Two hours that reset a week of souk walking.

images.alt: Vaulted bathhouse hall with hanging lanterns
Arched doorway inside a traditional building
Warmly lit vaulted passage with glass windows

experiences.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa night market food walk

host.name: Mehdi
host.bio: Grew up doing homework at his uncle's grill stall on the square. Knows which of the hundred numbered stands are for tourists and which three the stallholders themselves eat at.

experiences.description: When the sun drops, stall smoke rises and Jemaa el-Fnaa becomes the largest open-air dinner table in Africa. Grilled kefta and merguez, a bowl of harira, tanjia pulled from the ashes, snail broth for the brave, and chebakia with spiced coffee — navigated between the storytellers, gnawa musicians, and orange-juice carts.

images.alt: Marrakech square glowing with lights at night
Crowds moving across a large open plaza
Generous spread of dishes ready for eating

experiences.name: Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum with an art historian

host.name: Yasmine
host.bio: Marrakchi art historian who wrote her thesis on Jacques Majorelle's Atlas paintings. Former docent at the Musée Yves Saint Laurent, now leads small private visits.

experiences.description: Skip-the-line entry to the Jardin Majorelle at opening, before the crowds fill the bamboo walks. Yasmine unpacks the story behind that ultramarine blue, Majorelle's Atlas expeditions, and how Saint Laurent and Bergé saved the garden — finishing in the YSL museum's love-letter of a collection next door.

images.alt: Bright cobalt-blue building surrounded by lush greenery
Blue and yellow villa framed by palm trees
Garden path lined with many species of cactus

experiences.name: Hidden medina heritage walk: Medersa, fondouks, and fountains

host.name: Hicham
host.bio: Licensed national guide and restoration consultant who spent four years documenting the medina's surviving fondouks. Can read the city's history from a doorway.

experiences.description: The medina beyond the shopping: the carved cedar and stucco of the Medersa Ben Youssef, working fondouks where artisans still rent rooms above their workshops, the almoravid Koubba, and the mouassine fountains that watered the caravan city. Three hours that turn a maze into a map.

images.alt: Ornate courtyard of the Medersa Ben Youssef
People walking down a narrow medina street
Street scene beside old medina buildings

experiences.name: Mint tea ceremony and Moroccan pastry workshop

host.name: Souad
host.bio: Pastry chef who apprenticed under her aunts for wedding-season kaab el ghzal production. Pours tea from a full arm's height without losing a drop.

experiences.description: Learn why the first glass is bitter and the third is gentle: the full Moroccan tea ceremony, poured properly from height, alongside a hands-on pastry session — almond-paste kaab el ghzal, sesame ghriba, and honeyed chebakia. Everything you shape, you take home in a box.

images.alt: Tea being poured from a silver Moroccan teapot into a glass
Fresh mint leaves in clear tea glasses
Moroccan pastries in a bowl beside a teapot

experiences.name: High Atlas day trek from Imlil with mule support

host.name: Mohamed
host.bio: UIMLA-certified mountain leader from Aroumd village with over 200 Toubkal summits. Runs treks with his brothers and a very opinionated mule named Zniber.

experiences.description: Hotel pickup in Marrakech, then a full day on Atlas trails: up the Imlil valley through walnut and cherry orchards, over the Tizi n'Tamatert pass, and into the Imnane valley for lunch in a village house — grilled meats, salads, and tea with a family Mohamed has known all his life. Mule support carries the bags; you carry the views.

images.alt: Berber villages clinging to an Atlas mountainside
Aerial view of layered brown Atlas ridgelines
Guide with a horse on a green slope facing the mountains

experiences.name: Hot-air balloon at dawn over the palm groves

host.name: Karim
host.bio: Commercial balloon pilot with 2,400 flight hours over the Haouz plain. Flew his first Marrakech dawn in 2011 and still photographs every sunrise.

experiences.description: Pre-dawn pickup, mint tea while the envelope inflates, then an hour drifting silently over palm groves, Berber villages, and the dry Tensift riverbed as the sun clears the Atlas. Landing is celebrated the traditional way: Berber breakfast in a nomad tent and a flight certificate signed by the pilot.

images.alt: Hot air balloons floating above a desert landscape
Group of hot air balloons rising into the sky
Passengers riding in a hot air balloon basket

experiences.name: Agafay desert quad ride to a sunset camp
experiences.groupSize: Up to 10 guests, ages 16+ to drive

host.name: Ayoub
host.bio: Grew up racing motocross on the Haouz plain; now runs a small fleet of well-maintained quads out of a family camp on the edge of the Agafay.

experiences.description: Two hours of guided riding across the Agafay's lunar hills and dry wadis — proper briefing, helmets, and a pace set to the group — ending on a ridge camp for sunset over the Atlas. Mint tea, Berber pizza baked in the camp oven, and a headlit convoy back after dark.

images.alt: Rider on a quad bike crossing desert terrain
Group riding ATVs in a line across the desert
Desert landscape with low buildings and mountains behind

services.name: Rooftop restaurant overlooking Jemaa el-Fnaa

host.name: Restaurant Dar Lalla
host.bio: Family-run rooftop above the square since 1998, three generations in the kitchen. Tables on the top terrace book out for sunset a day or two ahead.

services.description: Three tiered terraces stacked above the square, with the top level looking straight across the smoke of the food stalls to the floodlit Koutoubia. Order the pastilla and the lamb tanjia, time it for the sunset call to prayer, and let the square's noise become the soundtrack to dinner.

images.alt: Terrace bar sign on a Marrakech rooftop
Metal tables and chairs on an upper-floor terrace
Illuminated restaurant sign above the square at night

services.name: Dar Yacout-style dinner in a candlelit riad

host.name: Dar Nejjarine
host.bio: A restored merchant's dar serving one seating a night. The dadas in the kitchen have cooked together for twenty years; the menu changes with the market, never with fashion.

services.description: Dinner as ceremony: you are collected from the nearest gate, led by lantern through the derbs, and seated in a candlelit courtyard for the classic progression — a constellation of cooked salads, pigeon pastilla, a slow tagine, couscous seffa, and orange blossom fruit. One seating, no menu, no wrong choices.

images.alt: Dining room with a table elegantly set for dinner
Moroccan salads and dishes arranged in bowls on a table
Table topped with generous plates of food

services.name: Pâtisserie Amandine: French-Moroccan patisserie in Gueliz

host.name: Pâtisserie Amandine
host.bio: Gueliz institution since 1999 with a French-trained pastry team and a Moroccan sweets counter. Locals queue on Sunday mornings; the salon de thé hums all day.

services.description: Two counters, one address: millefeuilles and lemon tarts on the French side, cornes de gazelle and honeyed briouats on the Moroccan side, and an avocado-almond smoothie that has its own fan club. Sit in the salon de thé with a nous-nous coffee and watch Gueliz go by.

services.name: Medina sweets house and tea room

host.name: Dar Cherifa Sweets
host.bio: A hole-in-the-wall counter with a tiny tiled tea room upstairs, run by two sisters who learned wedding pastry from their grandmother in the Kasbah quarter.

services.description: Trays of chebakia glazed in honey and sesame, almond ghriba cracked just right, sellou by the scoop, and kaab el ghzal shaped by hand each morning. Take a mixed box for the road or climb to the six-table tea room where the mint tea comes poured from height.

images.alt: Fresh pastries stacked on a brown tray
Moroccan pastries beside a traditional teapot
Glass of mint tea with fresh green leaves

services.name: Le Jardin Secret courtyard restaurant

host.name: Le Jardin d'Aziza
host.bio: A young Marrakchi chef returned from kitchens in Lyon and Beirut to cook her grandmother's repertoire with lighter hands, in a banana-palm courtyard hidden off the Mouassine souk.

services.description: A green pause in the middle of the souks: tables scattered under banana palms and bamboo, tortoises patrolling the tiles. The kitchen sends out reinvented classics — smoked-aubergine zaalouk, saffron chicken with charred lemon, a deconstructed pastilla — alongside proper fresh juices and a serious vegetarian page.

images.alt: Wooden dining tables set in a leafy courtyard
Bowl of Moroccan soup served at the table
Plate of food with vegetable sides

services.name: Spice-square rooftop café at Rahba Kedima

host.name: Café des Épices Rooftop
host.bio: The terrace above the old spice square, run by the same medina family for two decades. Waiters who remember your order from three years ago.

services.description: The classic perch above Rahba Kedima: baskets of spices and woven hats below, storks overhead, and the Atlas on the horizon on clear days. Come for a khobz-and-kefta sandwich or an avocado smoothie at lunch, stay for golden hour when the whole square turns amber.

images.alt: Black and white patio table and chairs on a terrace
Colorful goods displayed in the souk below
Moroccan teapot set on a tray outdoors

services.name: Palmeraie poolside lunch club

host.name: Les Palmiers Beldi Club
host.bio: A day-club and restaurant in an old palm-grove farm: olive trees, a long green-tiled pool, and a wood-fired grill that has anchored the menu since opening.

services.description: The Marrakech long lunch, perfected: a morning by the green-tiled pool under the palms, then grilled sea bream, lamb chops, and heaping market salads served at shaded farm tables. Day passes include a lounger and towel; book ahead on weekends when Marrakchi families claim the garden.

images.alt: Guest walking along the edge of a garden swimming pool
Platter of grilled meat and vegetables on a table
Palm tree beside a white and blue garden building

services.name: Tanjia and grill house in the Mellah

host.name: Chez Hamid Tanjia
host.bio: Hamid buries his tanjia urns in the farnatchi ashes at dawn, the way the bachelors of Marrakech have done for centuries. By 1pm the day's batch is spoken for.

services.description: The city's signature dish done the old way: lamb, preserved lemon, smen, and saffron sealed in clay urns and slow-cooked all morning in the ashes of the hammam furnace. Arrive before one, order tanjia with khobz and a tomato salad, and eat at shared tables with the market porters who set the standard.

images.alt: Bowl of slow-cooked Moroccan food on a table
Table spread with Moroccan dishes
Busy street scene in the old medina

services.name: Ourika riverside tagine terrace

host.name: Chez Lahcen au Bord de l'Eau
host.bio: Lahcen's family has cooked for valley travelers for forty years, at plastic tables set literally in the shallows of the Ourika river.

services.description: Lunch with your feet nearly in the river: tagines that have been burbling over charcoal since morning, salads from the family plot, and watermelon cooled in the current. No menu to speak of — beef with prunes or chicken with preserved lemon — and no better way to end a waterfall hike from Setti Fatma.

images.alt: Tagine of slow-cooked meat and vegetables
Valley houses surrounded by green trees

services.name: Kasbah panoramic terrace by the Saadian Tombs

host.name: Kasbah Café Terrasse
host.bio: Perched opposite the minaret of the Kasbah Mosque, steps from the Saadian Tombs. The upstairs tables catch the storks gliding to their nests on the palace walls at dusk.

services.description: The terrace every Kasbah visitor climbs to eventually — directly facing the tiled minaret of the Kasbah Mosque, with storks wheeling between the palace ramparts. Slow-roasted mechoui lamb on Fridays, reliable tagines all week, fresh juices, and the best people-watching south of the square.
